issues.evidence: Both channels sit on the wrong side of the antibody axis. R1_DMSO_EZH2 has pc1 -11.948 (pc1_z_within_antibody -23.366) and R1_DMSO_IgG has pc1 +12.609 (z 31.144). All other EZH2 channels have pc1 of about +11.4 to +13.4 and all other IgG channels about -11.6 to -12.9. PC1 separates antibody (association 0.667). Both channels also correlate poorly with the mean of their nominal antibody group: antibody_corr 0.878 (z -18.66) and 0.873 (z -19.868), against 0.961-0.970 for the other ten. The DMSO_1 paired ratio is also reversed: slope_vs_other_cultures -0.935 against +1.375 to +1.491 for the other five cultures, and median_ratio +0.146 against -0.115 to -0.210 elsewhere. The channels are not low-loading or low-depth: raw_median_z -0.42 and 0.795, n_quantified 1467 and 1472. The data are consistent with the EZH2 and IgG labels of culture DMSO_1 being exchanged.
issues.impact: The within-culture contrasts EZH2_vs_IgG_in_DMSO and interaction are affected, because the DMSO_1 pair enters with its sign reversed. With one of three DMSO replicates reversed, the DMSO EZH2-vs-IgG enrichment is attenuated and noisier. The interaction (CPI-169 EZH2/IgG minus DMSO EZH2/IgG) is then biased upward for EZH2-enriched proteins, so CPI-169 appears to increase EZH2 labelling, or to reduce it less than it truly does, and the bias reverses for IgG-enriched proteins. The between-culture contrasts CPI169_vs_DMSO_in_EZH2 and CPI169_vs_DMSO_in_IgG are also contaminated, because each DMSO group contains one channel from the other antibody. This inflates variance and biases both contrasts toward whichever antibody's profile the misplaced channel carries.
issues.recommendation: Check the TMT channel-to-sample assignment and the sample sheet for culture 1 DMSO, and the bead and tube handling records, to see whether the swap happened at labelling, at sample handling, or in annotation. If the records confirm a swap, correct the labels and re-run the analysis. If they do not, the metrics cannot separate a swap from a real biological difference or a failed enrichment in this culture. In that case, run the analysis with and without the DMSO_1 pair and report both, or exclude the pair, noting that the DMSO within-culture contrasts then rest on two cultures.

summary: One major problem: the antibody labels of the DMSO_1 pair (R1_DMSO_EZH2 and R1_DMSO_IgG) appear to be swapped. Both channels fall on the opposite antibody side of PC1, have very low antibody_corr_z (-18.66 and -19.87), and DMSO_1 has a negative paired-ratio slope (-0.935) where the other cultures show about +1.4. Loading and depth are normal for all channels, and no factor-wide loading imbalance is apparent (antibody means 20.196 vs 20.042, compound means 20.085 vs 20.152). The swap would distort the DMSO within-culture contrast and the interaction, and add noise to the between-culture contrasts. The sample sheet should be verified and the labels corrected before any differential analysis.
